items.text: People at a distance see what looks like a person; closer inspection makes it look like a rock. Which claim is closest to your view?

options.label: A rock was there independently of how anyone perceived it.
Something external may be there, but identifying it as a rock partly depends on how minds organize experience.
No rock or other object exists there independently of experience.
Changing appearances do not settle whether a mind-independent object is there.

items.notes: A concrete perceptual-error contrast for EP11 review. The first option would support ordinary-object mind-independence; the third would oppose it. The second and fourth must remain non-directional because external existence, conceptual organization, and skeptical suspension differ. Authored content independence from EPI037 is a hypothesis requiring review, not an empirical finding.
